chapter: Arranging for other bandleaders and closing talk
title: Millinder's cab fare trick and the knife-wielding driver
summary: Millinder ran up cab meters and left drivers waiting; when one threatened him with a knife at the Savoy, his bandsmen bet he'd talk his way out, and he did.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

-- and the guys that worked with Lucky Millender that are living today know this as a fact. So one day this particular cab driver, I found out, found out that Lucky Millender was playing at the Savoy. So this cab driver caught him one night just before he got ready to go upstairs, you know, and he grabbed him, and here some of the other guys in the band were getting ready to come up. And this cab driver had one of these long jack knives and reared back to hit Lucky unless he was going to give him his money. You know what the guys in the band were doing? They were betting two to one that Lucky Millender wouldn't (unintelligible) get hit and--
-- would talk himself out of it.

Do you know, after the cab driver and he were talking for about five minutes, do you know what happened? This is funny and this is the truth. The cab driver put down his handle -- jack handle what he had, went in his pocket and gave Lucky some money.

I'm telling you, this is what happened. And sure enough, Lucky put a story

on him that was so bad -- I don't know what it was -- but the guys bet on it because they knew. This was Lucky Millinder. But he was a great performer, and he'd tell you, 'I'll be right back, I'll be right back.' You can kiss him goodbye. You won't see him anymore.

So I haven't seen or heard of that guy in years. I don't know -- those guys live forever, though, that do these things. If it were you or if it was me, man, we'd be in the grave, you know. So that's the story on Lucky Millinder. I thought I had to tell that. But that isn't a joke. That's a fact.
